speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your specific symptoms regarding the gait and limb ataxia you mentioned, and list your significant medical history so I can begin my assessment.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the sensation of looking "drunk" and clumsiness on the right side is concerning for a focal neurological issue. Given your significant medical history, have you been diagnosed with multiple sclerosis or suffered any prior strokes? Additionally, do you experience any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your limbs alongside the ataxia?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, a medication known to increase the risk of PML, I need to confirm if you have experienced any new or worsening neurological symptoms like vision changes, confusion, or weakness recently. I am requesting an MRI of your brain to look for characteristic white matter lesions.
